item.title: Our Story
item.dc:creator: agave
item.content:encoded:
Some recipes are written down. Ours was handed down — tasted, adjusted and perfected around a family table long before it ever reached a plancha in San Diego.

Born from birria

Agave began with one dish: birria de res, the slow-braised, chile-red stew from Jalisco that turns a simple taco into a ritual. Our founder, Juan Pablo Oceguera, first shared that family recipe with North County at Agave Birrieria in Encinitas. The response was immediate — lines out the door, regulars on a first-name basis and a city asking for more.

So we brought the birria south to Point Loma. At 4111 West Point Loma Boulevard, Agave Taco Shop became the neighborhood spot where surfers grab breakfast burritos at 7 AM, families share birria fries on the patio and night owls chase the perfect quesabirria until midnight on weekends.

“No shortcuts. If it takes all night to braise the birria, then it takes all night.”

— The Agave kitchen rule

What we believe

🔥

Slow food, served fast

Our birria braises for hours so your order can be ready in minutes — at the counter, the drive-thru or your door.

🌶

Scratch-made, daily

Salsas, consommé, guacamole and aguas frescas are made in-house every single day.

🤝

Family hospitality

Generous portions, friendly faces and a “welcome back” every time you return.

🌊

Point Loma proud

Minutes from Ocean Beach, Liberty Station and the Midway District — your neighborhood taco shop.

Our journey

  • The family tableA birria recipe passed down through generations, built on dried chiles, patience and love.
  • 2021 · Agave Birrieria, EncinitasThe first Agave opens in North County and quickly becomes a birria destination.
  • 2022 · Agave Taco Shop, Point LomaWe open on West Point Loma Blvd with a full taco shop menu, breakfast from 7 AM and a drive-thru.
  • TodayServing San Diego from sunrise to late night, plus catering for parties, offices and celebrations across the county.

Come hungry

Whether it is your first quesabirria or your hundredth California burrito, we cannot wait to feed you. Explore the menu, find us in Point Loma or bring Agave to your next event.

Yes. Bean and cheese burritos, cheese quesadillas, veggie-friendly sides, rice, beans, guacamole and fresh salsas are available for every package.

Do you deliver catering orders in San Diego?

Pickup in Point Loma is always available. Delivery and on-site setup may be available depending on date, distance and group size — just ask when you request your quote.

How is the birria kept hot?

Birria and consommé are packed in insulated containers so you can serve them hot and fresh. We include simple serving instructions with every order.

item.title: What Is Quesabirria? San Diego’s Guide to the Cheesiest Taco on Earth
item.dc:creator: agave
item.content:encoded:
If you have scrolled through food videos in the last few years, you have seen it: a crispy, red-tinted taco pulled apart in a stretch of melted cheese, then dunked into a cup of steaming broth. That is quesabirria — and San Diego is one of the best places in the country to eat it.

Quesabirria, defined

Quesabirria is a mash-up of two words: queso (cheese) and birria (a slow-braised, chile-rich meat stew). In practice it is a taco — or a taco-quesadilla hybrid — made with tender birria and melted cheese, crisped on a griddle and served with a cup of consommé, the flavorful broth the meat was cooked in.

Three things make a great quesabirria:

  • The birria. Beef marinated in an adobo of dried chiles such as guajillo and ancho, garlic, oregano and warm spices, then braised for hours until it shreds with a fork.
  • The tortilla. Corn tortillas are dipped in the red fat that rises to the top of the pot, then griddled until crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle.
  • The consommé. A rich, savory broth for dipping every single bite — finished with onion, cilantro and lime.

Where does birria come from?

Birria is a traditional dish from the Mexican state of Jalisco, where it has been served at celebrations for generations. It was originally made with goat, while beef birria (birria de res) became the star in Tijuana's taco stands. From there, the quesabirria trend crossed the border and exploded across Southern California — and San Diego, just minutes from Tijuana, has been at the center of it ever since.

How to eat quesabirria like a local

  1. Squeeze lime over the taco and add a spoonful of salsa.
  2. Dip the taco straight into the consommé — do not be shy.
  3. Bite, then sip. Many fans drink the consommé between tacos like a soup.
  4. Repeat until the cup is empty (it will happen faster than you think).

Pro tip: order an extra consommé. You will want it for the last taco.

Quesabirria vs. birria tacos: what is the difference?

All quesabirria are birria tacos, but not every birria taco has cheese. A classic taco de birria is meat, onion and cilantro on a dipped tortilla. Quesabirria adds a layer of melted cheese that crisps on the griddle — making it richer, crunchier and, for many people, irresistible.

Where to get the best quesabirria in San Diego

At Agave Taco Shop in Point Loma, quesabirria is our fan favorite. Our birria is marinated overnight, slow-braised in-house and served with the consommé from the same pot. Order the Quesabirria Combo with rice and beans, try it in a burrito, or go all-in with birria fries.

We are at 4111 W Point Loma Blvd, open from 7 AM daily and until midnight on weekends — with a drive-thru for when the craving cannot wait.

item.title: The Best Birria Tacos in San Diego: Why Point Loma Lines Up at Agave
item.dc:creator: agave
item.content:encoded:
San Diego takes its tacos seriously. With Tijuana just across the border and a taco shop on nearly every corner, “best” is a bold word. So let us talk about what actually makes birria great — and you can be the judge.

1. The chiles

Great birria starts with a deep, layered adobo. Dried guajillo chiles bring bright red color and gentle fruitiness; ancho adds a raisin-like sweetness and body. Toasted, soaked and blended with garlic, oregano, cumin and warm spices, they create a marinade that is rich without being punishingly hot.

2. Time

There is no fast birria. Beef rests overnight in the adobo and then braises low and slow for hours. That patience is what turns tough, flavorful cuts into meat that falls apart — and builds the consommé at the same time.

3. The consommé

If the birria is the heart, the consommé is the soul. A great consommé is glossy, savory and deeply beefy, with a gentle chile warmth. It should taste good enough to drink on its own — because many people do.

4. The griddle

The final step happens on the plancha. Tortillas are dipped in the fat skimmed from the pot and crisped until golden. Add cheese and you get quesabirria — crunchy, stretchy and impossible to stop eating.

Why Point Loma lines up at Agave

  • A family recipe, first perfected at our sister restaurant Agave Birrieria in Encinitas.
  • Made in-house daily — the birria, the consommé, the salsas and the aguas frescas.
  • Birria every way: quesabirria tacos, birria burritos, birria quesadillas, birria fries and full plates.
  • Convenient: open 7 AM daily, until midnight Friday and Saturday, with a drive-thru and patio.
  • Easy to find: 4111 W Point Loma Blvd — minutes from Ocean Beach, Midway, Loma Portal and Liberty Station.

What to order on your first visit

Start with the Quesabirria Combo: two quesabirria tacos, rice, beans and consommé. Bringing friends? Add birria fries for the table and a round of horchata and jamaica.

Ready? Order online for pickup or swing through the drive-thru.

item.title: How to Eat Birria Like a Pro: The Consommé Dip, Explained
item.dc:creator: agave
item.content:encoded:
Your tray arrives: crispy red tacos, a cup of steaming broth, a pile of onion and cilantro, a wedge of lime. Now what? Here is the Agave guide to eating birria like you grew up on it.

Step 1: Dress the consommé

Before you touch a taco, give the consommé a squeeze of lime and a pinch of onion and cilantro. Taste it. Want more heat? Add a little salsa roja right into the cup.

Step 2: Dip with confidence

Hold the taco firmly by the bottom and dip the tip straight into the consommé. A quick dunk keeps the tortilla crispy; a long soak makes it soft and juicy. Both are correct.

Step 3: Bite, sip, repeat

Take a bite, then a sip of consommé. The broth resets your palate and warms you up for the next taco. Many regulars save the final few sips to drink at the end — consider it dessert.

Toppings and salsa pairings

  • Salsa verde brings tangy brightness that cuts through the richness.
  • Salsa roja doubles down on smoky chile flavor.
  • Pickled onions or radishes add crunch and acidity.
  • Extra lime is never a mistake.

What to drink with birria

Birria is rich, so you want something refreshing. Our horchata — creamy rice and cinnamon — cools the chile heat, while tart jamaica (hibiscus) cleanses the palate. A glass-bottle Mexican soda is a classic too.

Common birria mistakes

  1. Letting it sit. Birria tacos are best within minutes of leaving the griddle. If you are taking them home, keep the consommé separate and dip just before eating.
  2. Skipping the consommé. It is half the experience.
  3. Ordering only one. Trust us.

Try it at Agave

Put your new skills to the test at Agave Taco Shop, 4111 W Point Loma Blvd. Order the Quesabirria Combo and ask for extra consommé — we will not judge.

In San Diego, the breakfast burrito is not just a meal — it is a lifestyle. It fits in one hand, survives a drive to the beach and keeps you full through a long session in the water or a busy morning at work.

Why San Diego runs on breakfast burritos

Southern California's taco shops made the breakfast burrito a local institution: eggs, potatoes, cheese and your choice of meat, wrapped tight in a warm flour tortilla and ready in minutes. It is portable, affordable and endlessly customizable — exactly what a beach city needs at sunrise.

The Agave breakfast lineup

Our doors — and our drive-thru — open at 7 AM every day. Here is what our early regulars order:

  • Bacon Breakfast Burrito — bacon, crispy potatoes, scrambled egg and cheese. The undisputed morning hero.
  • Chorizo & Egg Burrito — spiced chorizo, eggs, potatoes and cheese for bold flavor.
  • Carnitas & Egg Burrito — slow-cooked pork with eggs and salsa. Hearty and satisfying.
  • Bean, Egg & Cheese Burrito — a vegetarian classic that never disappoints.

Order tip: ask for salsa roja and salsa verde on the side, so you can switch it up bite to bite.

The perfect pre-beach stop

Agave Taco Shop is on West Point Loma Boulevard, just minutes from Ocean Beach, Dog Beach and Sunset Cliffs. Roll through the drive-thru, grab your burrito and still catch the morning glass-off.

Breakfast for the whole crew

Feeding a team, a youth sports squad or an early office meeting? Our breakfast burrito trays come individually wrapped and labeled, ready as early as 7 AM.

Order ahead

Skip the morning line: order online and pick up hot at 4111 W Point Loma Blvd.

item.title: The California Burrito: A San Diego Icon (and Where to Get a Great One)
item.dc:creator: agave
item.content:encoded:
Ask a San Diegan for one dish that defines their city, and there is a good chance the answer will be the California burrito. It is big, it is unapologetic and it has french fries inside.

What is a California burrito?

A California burrito wraps carne asada, french fries or crispy potatoes, cheese and usually sour cream (and sometimes guacamole or pico de gallo) in a large flour tortilla. It combines the smoky char of grilled steak with the salty comfort of fries — a combination that makes perfect sense the moment you take a bite.

A San Diego original

The California burrito is widely credited to San Diego's taco shops, where it became a late-night and post-surf staple. Today you will find it across the Southwest, but San Diego still considers it a hometown dish — and debates about who makes the best one never really end.

How to spot a great California burrito

  • Well-seasoned carne asada with real char, chopped fresh.
  • Crispy potatoes — never soggy.
  • Balance: enough cheese and sour cream to bind everything, not drown it.
  • A tight wrap that holds together to the last bite.
  • Salsa on the side so you can control the heat.

The Agave California Burrito

Ours is built the San Diego way: charred carne asada, crispy potatoes, melted cheese and sour cream, wrapped warm and ready to travel. Want to go further? Try the Birria Burrito and dip it in consommé — a Point Loma twist on a classic.

Where to get one

Agave Taco Shop, 4111 W Point Loma Blvd, San Diego. Open from 7 AM daily and until midnight Friday and Saturday — because California burrito cravings do not keep business hours. See all burritos.

item.title: Taco Catering in San Diego: The Complete Party Planning Guide
item.dc:creator: agave
item.content:encoded:
Nothing gets a San Diego crowd excited like a taco bar. It is colorful, interactive, works for almost every diet and feels like a party the moment the lids come off. Here is how to plan it right.

How many tacos per person?

A reliable rule of thumb for taco catering:

  • Lunch or light meal: 2–3 tacos per guest
  • Dinner or main event: 3–4 tacos per guest
  • Hungry crowds (teams, teenagers, long parties): plan for 4–5

Adding rice, beans and chips? You can lean toward the lower end. Not sure? We will recommend quantities when you request a quote.

Taco bar, birria bar or burrito boxes?

  • Birria Bar: the showstopper. Guests build quesabirria tacos and dip them in hot consommé. Perfect for birthdays and celebrations.
  • Street Taco Bar: the crowd pleaser. Choose carne asada, carnitas, pollo asado or birria with all the toppings.
  • Burrito Boxes: the meeting MVP. Individually wrapped, labeled and easy to hand out — ideal for offices and game days.
  • Breakfast Trays: early meetings and morning events, ready as early as 7 AM.

Plan for every guest

Include vegetarian options such as bean and cheese burritos or cheese quesadillas, and keep salsas on the side so guests can choose their heat level. Label everything — your guests will thank you.

Timing tips

  1. Book early: at least 72 hours ahead, and one to two weeks for weekends and large groups.
  2. Schedule pickup 15–30 minutes before you plan to serve.
  3. Keep it hot: leave insulated containers closed until serving.
  4. Serve the consommé last-minute for the best birria experience.

Do not forget the drinks

Gallons of horchata and jamaica turn a meal into a fiesta — and they are a welcome alcohol-free option for every guest.

Book your taco catering with Agave

From Point Loma and Liberty Station to Downtown, Mission Valley and beyond, Agave Taco Shop caters parties of every size. Request your catering quote or call (619) 230-5282.

The concert just ended. The game went to overtime. Your friends are hungry and nobody wants fast food. Good news: Agave Taco Shop is open until midnight every Friday and Saturday.

The late-night menu, ranked by cravings

  • Carne asada fries — built for sharing (or not).
  • California burrito — San Diego's official after-hours meal.
  • Birria fries — the best of both worlds.

Perfectly located for a night out

Agave Taco Shop is on West Point Loma Boulevard, minutes from the Midway District and the arena area, Ocean Beach nightlife and Liberty Station. Easy parking and a drive-thru mean you can be eating in minutes.

Weeknights too

Late-night ordering tips

  2. Use the drive-thru if you are heading home.
